note: Hebrew esh zarah is fire that is "foreign" to the prescribed ritual, i.e. not authorized; modern "strange" suggests merely odd.
Hebrew zar here means anyone not of the authorized group (a non-priest/non-Levite, even an Israelite), not a foreigner as modern "stranger" implies; same in 3:38.
Hebrew menorah is a stand holding oil lamps; there were no candles. Recurs throughout.
Hebrew qerashim are now generally understood as open wooden frames rather than solid planks.
